run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: I could not resolve request REQ-EU-8K4M2 or name the service that served it slowly. The two sources that could carry per-request evidence were unreachable for the whole run: every Jaeger call (traces_list_services, traces_search, traces_search_by_tags) and every Prometheus call (get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, list_prometheus_rules, get_prometheus_target) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for target m0-otel-20260909, so no span, error-rate or latency series were read. Elasticsearch was reachable but its 1620 app-185-geo-* indices contain only one uniform synthetic record per service/region/day (level INFO, message "Request completed successfully", response_time_ms 150 for every region including eu-west and eu-central), and a search of the request_id field for REQ-EU-8K4M2 returned nothing. Kubernetes shows a node-wide sandbox restart at 04:23:42Z-04:23:46Z (all otel-demo containers terminated with exit code 255/reason Unknown, SandboxChanged then Created/Started for every pod), brief DNS failures (ad could not resolve flagd and otel-collector until ~04:24:25Z) and startup-only probe misses; by query time all 21 deployments were 1/1 ready and all 33 pods Running, and every flagd feature flag was set to variant off. That restart plausibly explains why the telemetry backends restarted (and Jaeger logged itself ready at 04:23:48Z), but nothing in the available evidence ties it to the customer's slow request, so no root cause is asserted and the assessment is incomplete.

claims.text: In the authorized 24h window Elasticsearch returned 162 documents, all of level INFO with the single message "Request completed successfully", spread over 6 regions (including eu-west and eu-central) and 27 service values, with response_time_ms uniformly 150 (min, max and average all 150).
Only index app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05 maps request-level fields (request_id, endpoint, user_id); it is also the only index in the cluster holding 2 documents rather than 1.

Namespace otel-demo recorded 98 events between 2026-11-21T04:23:46Z and 04:24:34Z: every application pod has a SandboxChanged event ("Pod sandbox changed, it will be killed and re-created") at 04:23:46Z followed by Pulled/Created/Started; the only Unhealthy/BackOff events belong to kube-state-metrics-7cbf5b996-df4sz, otel-collector-789c64b9bf-tl55c and prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn during their startup.

The containers that host the telemetry backends were terminated at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exit code 255 and reason Unknown (jaeger, opentelemetry-collector and prometheus-server), and the prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx exited with code 1 at 04:24:10Z before starting again at 04:24:34Z; event grouping also shows Node-level "Starting" events at 04:23:43Z.
At query time all 21 otel-demo deployments reported desired 1, available 1 and ready 1, and all 33 pods in the cluster were phase Running and ready (application pods with restartCount 1).

The flagd-config ConfigMap (demo.flagd.json) has every flag enabled in state but with defaultVariant "off" at query time, including imageSlowLoad (variants 10sec/5sec/off), paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, kafkaQueueProblems and loadGeneratorFloodHomepage.
The ad pod logged java.net.UnknownHostException failures resolving flagd:8013 and otel-collector between 04:23:55Z and 04:24:25Z, immediately after the sandbox restart.

The frontend container's stdout in the observed hour contains only 12 Next.js startup lines ("Ready in 703ms" and a Node MetadataLookupWarning); no request-handling line and no REQ-EU-8K4M2 line appears in it.
The Jaeger pod restarted at 04:23:48Z and logged "Health Check state change", status ready, "Query server started" on 16686 and "Starting GRPC server" on 16685.
Namespace app-101 received ConfigMaps loki-config and promtail-config with creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T04:59:05Z, i.e. after the authorized window ended, alongside a running Loki pod.

The simultaneous termination of every otel-demo container at 04:23:42Z (exit 255, reason Unknown) with SandboxChanged events and Node "Starting" events is a node/sandbox-level restart that also restarted Jaeger, the otel-collector and Prometheus, explaining the brief DNS and exporter failures; whether it is connected to the customer's slow request is unverified.

The fault-injection surface I could read does not show an active latency injection: all flagd flag variants are set to off at query time, and no deployment carries a change-cause or non-default revision annotation (all deployments are revision 1). This is the current object state and cannot prove what the flags were earlier in the window.

A configuration-only rollout caused the 04:23 restart: rejected, because every otel-demo ReplicaSet was created on 2026-11-20T16:32:06/07 with unchanged image tags, no new ReplicaSet appeared, and the restarted pods kept the same ReplicaSet names, so the restart was a sandbox/node-level event rather than a template rollout.

Restore the Jaeger and Prometheus read paths for target m0-otel-20260909 (the Jaeger pod logged itself ready at 04:23:48Z, so the outage is on the query path, not the backend pod), then look the request up by its request-id tag to identify the slow span and service.

Once the Loki instance in namespace app-101 has collected logs covering the incident window, search it for REQ-EU-8K4M2 and for the eu-west region, since the Elasticsearch indices available in this run contain no such request id.

gaps: Jaeger was unreachable for the entire run: traces_list_services, traces_search (frontend), traces_search_by_tags and traces_list_services all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span, trace id or request-id tag exists in this evidence and the specific request REQ-EU-8K4M2 could not be resolved.

Prometheus was unreachable for the entire run: get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query (up, 1), metrics_range_query, list_prometheus_rules and get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency or kube-state-metrics series were read and no service can be named as slow; this is unknown, not zero.

The literal request id was not found in Elasticsearch: a match_phrase on request_id for REQ-EU-8K4M2 returned no documents, a wildcard on message.keyword for *REQ-EU* returned no documents, and the full-text query REQ-EU-8K4M2 only matched generic "Request completed successfully" documents by loose token matching (54 hits) that carry no request id.

The only index whose mapping contains request_id (app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05, 2 documents) returned no documents inside the 24h window, so its records could not be read; I could not determine whether they concern this request.

The 162 Elasticsearch documents visible in the window look synthetic and uniform (one message, response_time_ms 150 for every region and service), so their relation to the customer's European slow request is unknown.

The trigger of the mass container termination at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (exit code 255, reason Unknown) is not established: no node-level reason event beyond Node "Starting" was recorded, and the kubelet/node restart cause is unknown.

Whether any service actually returned slow or failed responses during the window was not verified: application stdout shows no request-level lines (frontend logs only startup output) and error-filtered reads of checkout, cart, shipping, email and image-provider returned no matching lines, which is not proof of absence.
The Loki/promtail stack in namespace app-101 was created at 04:59:05Z, after the incident window, and no Loki query tool is available in this run, so those logs could not be consulted.
The change_history integration is not available in this run, so no deployment/configuration change record for the window could be checked.
